newsitem.title: UK: Eurotunnel's troubled path to debt relief.
newsitem.headline: Eurotunnel's troubled path to debt relief.

text.p: Anglo-French Channel Tunnel operator Eurotunnel finally announced details of a debt restructuring deal with its creditor banks on Monday.

The proposals, which took more than a year to hammer out, give the banks 45.5 percent of the company, crowning almost a decade of troubled times since investors first put up cash for the ambitious project.
Key dates:
- 1802. Plans submitted to French Emperor Napoleon for a carriageway in a channel tunnel
- 1872. Channel Tunnel Co set up in Britain but work abandoned in 1883 after shafts and short tunnel stretch dug
- 1964. French and British governments decide to build tunnel and accept outline proposals by contractors in 1971
- 1974. France ratifies treaty on tunnel but Britain fails to follow suit because of general election
- 20 Jan 1986. French and British governments select Eurotunnel twin-bore rail tunnel out of four fixed link proposals
- 29 Oct 1986. Eurotunnel raises 206 million pounds in private institutional equity placement. Consortium partners earlier subscribed to 46 million pounds in equity
- 12 May 1987. European Investment Bank (EIB) agrees to lend 1.0 billion pounds ($1.56 billion) to tunnel project
- 29 July 1987. French and British leaders, meeting in Paris, ratify Channel Fixed Link Treaty giving Eurotunnel 55-year concession to run tunnel (later extended to 65 years)
- 4 Nov 1987. Banks provide loans for 1.0 billion pounds
- 27 Nov 1987. Eurotunnel share issue raises 770 million pounds
- 1 Dec 1987. Tunnelling begins at British side
- 2 Oct 1989. Eurotunnel says project costs have increased 40 percent to 7.0 billion pounds, will have to seek more funds.
- 8 Jan 1990. Contracting consortium TML takes Eurotunnel to court over unpaid bills
- 16 Feb 1990. French court orders Eurotunnel to pay 62 million pounds. Eurotunnel says unable to pay, project in jeopardy
- 28 May 1990. EIB provides 300 million pounds in loans
- 25 Oct 1990. Group of 200-plus banks provide additional credit
- 1 Dec 1990. Tunnel breakthrough.
- 3 Dec 1990. Eurotunnel rights issue raises 566 million pounds
- 28 June 1991. Main tunnelling work completed
- 6 Nov 1991. Loan from European Coal and Steel Community
- 27 Nov 1992. Crucial bank waiver on 6.8 billion pounds debts
- 17 May 1993. Channel Tunnel terminal opens at Waterloo, London
- 20 June 1993. Test train makes first tunnel trip.
- 21 April 1994. Eurotunnel seeks cash from British Rail and SNCF for tunnel passenger services delays
- 6 May 1994. Official opening of tunnel by French President Francois Mitterrand and Britain's Queen Elizabeth.
- 19 May 1994. "Le Shuttle" freight truck service opens.
- 26 May 1994. Eurotunnel sets 1.51 billion-pound refinancing
- 17 Oct 1994. Warns start-up delays will cut 1994 revenue
- 14 Nov 1994. Eurostar service officially opens
- 22 Dec "Le Shuttle" car-and-passenger service opens.
- 10 April 1995. Eurotunnel reports 1994 loss of 387 million pounds and warns: "Our debt-service costs may overwhelm us."
- 1 June 1995. Claims to lead freight truck market
- 5 Sept 1995. Claims becoming biggest Dover-Calais car carrier
- 14 Sept 1995. Freezes debt payments for up to 18 months.
- 6 Oct 1995. Eurotunnel announces first half loss of 465 million pounds but forecasts rising revenues
- 31 Oct 1995. Claims against SNCF and British Rail rejected
- 10 Jan 1996. Says expects sharply higher sales for 1996 and dismisses market talk of bankruptcy.
- 12 Feb 1996. Mediators appointed in debt talks.
- 22 April 1996. Reports net loss of 925 million stg for 1995 and warns cashflow may never pay off debts and interest.
- 3 June 1996. Patrick Ponsolle to be sole executive chairman as Sir Alastair Morton due to retire after debt deal agreed.
- 27 June 1996. Says breaking even, before interest and tax, in three months to end of May 1996.
- 9 Sept 1996. Eurotunnel says net loss for first half of 1996 narrows to 372 million stg. Morton to retire end October.
- 30 Sept 1996. Eurotunnel asks for temporary share suspension
- 7 Oct 1996. Eurotunnel unveils debt restructuring plan, says expects shares to resume trading October 8.
